correctness.rationale: The carrier lemma is proved for every graph of girth at least seven using the exclusion of closed walks that would create cycles of length at most six. Every non-edge-carrier face is private to exactly one star carrier and admits a genuine descending free-face pairing; the surviving union of full edge-fiber simplices collapses by dominated vertices to the fixed-color embedded graph. Exact counts follow from complete face partitions and intersection counts. The rank and integral split are established by the scale-one contractible-fiber graph model and the fixed-row homology section. The standalone independent-face-enumeration verifier tested the complete collapse in 22 finite instances, including branching intersecting cycles; no extrapolation from these checks is needed for the proof.

originality.rationale: The verified statement is an unbounded-width (m>=3), arbitrary finite high-girth base-graph scale-two Rips collapse with an exact elementary-pair formula and a split integral scale-one kernel. The closest full RESULT.md sources handle arbitrary base only at fiber width two, arbitrary width only for cycle bases, and arbitrary width/base for a Čech rather than Rips nerve. The 2025 primary torus-grid manuscript treats cyclic grid products and does not imply the arbitrary-base product. Exact claims and implications, not title similarity, were compared. Unindexed equivalents remain a real priority risk.
residual_risks: The existing high-girth K_2 proof uses an allied carrier-matching strategy; mathematical priority depends on whether a previously unpublished or unindexed arbitrary-m theorem exists.
The SoCG 2018 metric-gluing full text was not inspected; abstract-only information does not certify noncoverage.
Published or independent work under an alternate terminology might prove a stronger graph-square collapse.

value.rationale: An arbitrarily high-dimensional clique-fiber graph metric thickening can retain exactly the arbitrary high-girth base topology and forget every extra first-homology generator at one fixed scale. The theorem gives a complete infinite-family simplicial collapse, sharp girth boundary, exact elementary-pair complexity and primitive integral early persistence for any branching and interacting long cycles. It simultaneously extends two previously orthogonal restricted Rips domains and sharply contrasts with the same family under the Čech nerve, which has extra S2 summands. This is a natural structural stability question, not an arbitrary slice, code-only enumeration or restatement of a known specific result.
